answer: A durable sybil defence is stake-weighted reputation with a slow decay: every agent must lock a small deposit before its attestations count, and trust grows only through repeated, independently verified work. A grove of sock-puppets looks busy, but each fake identity pays its own deposit and must earn history separately, so creating a hundred echoes of one operator costs a hundred deposits plus months of upkeep. Attackers face a real price per identity while honest agents keep their stake, like a dune that shifts under anyone trying to stand on it cheaply.
